en: The Tamaraw, endemic to Mindoro, has distinctive V-shaped horns and is critically endangered.
The Waling-waling orchid, known as the Queen of Philippine Orchids, grows on trees in Mount Kitanglad.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to help premature babies survive in rural areas.
The Philippine Eagle lays only one egg per breeding cycle, making its population growth very slow.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects hundreds of fish species and diverse coral ecosystems.
The red mangrove grows specialized stilt roots that anchor it in muddy coastal soils and filter salt.
The Philippine mouse-deer uses its tiny size to hide from predators in the dense forests of Balabac.
The Aedes aegypti mosquito transmits the dengue virus to humans primarily by biting during early morning and late afternoon.
Golden Rice is genetically modified to produce beta-carotene, which the human body converts into vitamin A to prevent blindness.
The critically endangered Philippine crocodile builds nest mounds out of vegetation where its eggs incubate and hatch.
The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes fixed in its skull, requiring it to rotate its head 180 degrees to see.
Rafflesia schadenbergiana, a rare Philippine parasitic plant, produces massive flowers that emit a foul odor to attract pollinating flies.
